bibl.title: A novel visuospatial priming task for rats with relevance to Tourette syndrome and modulation of dopamine levels

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: In summary, we describe a novel visuospatial priming task that detects negative priming in rats.

span.label: negative visuospatial priming
span.quote: NP is the normal reduction of performance when identifying target stimuli that appears where non-target stimuli appeared previously.

span.label: behavioural-experiment
span.quote: Performance was challenged by shortening prime duration and by administering amphetamine.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: An inverted-U relation between dopamine transmission and inhibitory processing: amphetamine pushes low-NP animals toward and high-NP animals past an optimum, so the same drug raises or abolishes priming depending on baseline state
span.quote: The finding that AMPH improves NP in animals with normally low levels of NP, while reducing NP in animals with high levels of NP, suggests that an optimal level of dopamine transmission might produce maximal amount of negative visuospatial priming, and that levels either above or below that optimal point result in reduced or no negative priming.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Brief primes are routed through preconscious, automatic processing, which is the route that generates negative priming; longer primes recruit more controlled processing and weaken it
span.quote: Conceivably, shorter duration primes may favor processing by preconscious/automatic mechanisms, which may be required for the negative priming effect.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A species difference in speed-accuracy strategy - rats protect response speed and sacrifice accuracy - channels the priming cost into accuracy rather than latency
span.quote: The tendency of rats to maintain speed of responding at the cost of accuracy may therefore explain why the NP effect in our task primarily impacted response accuracy rather than response latencies.

span.label: Rats that could not acquire stable performance had to be dropped, reducing the sample.
span.quote: Three of 16 rats failed to develop stable performance in the task and were excluded, leading to a final n of 13 rats.

span.label: The task's whole-body response makes it insensitive to the tens-of-milliseconds latency effects that carry negative priming in humans.
span.quote: Changes in response latency on that scale would be difficult to detect in this rat NP task, which requires the rat to make a whole-body movement across the experimental chamber to respond to the stimulus.

span.label: No animal model, including this one, can capture the full neurobiology of the varied forms of Tourette syndrome.
span.quote: perhaps more importantly, no animal model is likely to capture the full neurobiology relevant to all of the varied forms of TS.

span.label: the Yerkes-Dodson inverted-U law, imported to explain why the same amphetamine dose helps low-NP and harms high-NP rats
span.quote: This “rate-dependent” effect of AMPH recalls the widely observed pattern described in the Yerkes-Dodson law, which states that performance, especially in difficult tasks, initially increases with physiological or mental arousal, but when levels of arousal become too high, performance is degraded

span.label: target and non-target locations varied pseudorandomly, equal counts per location per session, with location unpredictable
span.note: eliminates: a location bias and an anticipation strategy - the same design as the 2015 sister paper, and the same two-part justification
span.quote: The location of the target and non-target stimuli varied pseudorandomly between trials, so that each location contained the stimuli an equal number of times per session, but their location was not predictable on any given trial.

span.label: negative priming
span.quote: Individuals with Tourette syndrome (TS) exhibit deficits in inhibitory information processing which may reflect impaired neural mechanisms underlying symptoms and can be detected using a negative priming (NP) task. NP is the normal reduction of performance when identifying target stimuli that appears where non-target stimuli appeared previously. TS subjects exhibit diminished NP and their NP levels predict their response to behavioral therapy

span.label: inhibitory information processing
span.quote: Individuals with Tourette syndrome (TS) exhibit deficits in inhibitory information processing which may reflect impaired neural mechanisms underlying symptoms and can be detected using a negative priming (NP) task. NP is the normal reduction of performance when identifying target stimuli that appears where non-target stimuli appeared previously. TS subjects exhibit diminished NP and their NP levels predict their response to behavioral therapy

span.label: Tourette syndrome
span.quote: Individuals with Tourette syndrome (TS) exhibit deficits in inhibitory information processing which may reflect impaired neural mechanisms underlying symptoms and can be detected using a negative priming (NP) task. NP is the normal reduction of performance when identifying target stimuli that appears where non-target stimuli appeared previously. TS subjects exhibit diminished NP and their NP levels predict their response to behavioral therapy

span.label: prime duration
span.quote: Because the shortened 0.25 s prime stimulus duration produced the most robust negative priming in the previous experiments, this prime duration was used during the amphetamine challenge days

span.label: amphetamine
span.quote: Because the shortened 0.25 s prime stimulus duration produced the most robust negative priming in the previous experiments, this prime duration was used during the amphetamine challenge days

span.label: NEGATIVE PRIMING - a priming effect defined as a LOSS, and defined as the NORMAL one: `NP is the normal reduction of performance when identifying target stimuli that appears where non-target stimuli appeared previously.` Second record tonight whose priming effect harms performance (after Keane2015's costs), and the first where the harm is the healthy result
span.quote: NP is the normal reduction of performance when identifying target stimuli that appears where non-target stimuli appeared previously. TS subjects exhibit diminished NP

span.label: LESS PRIMING IS THE DEFICIT - the direction that inverts everything. `TS subjects exhibit DIMINISHED NP`, so a smaller effect is the pathological finding and a larger one is intact function. Any summary that treats priming magnitude as one quantity with a good direction gets this record backwards, and the corpus contains many records where more priming is the notable result
span.quote: NP is the normal reduction of performance when identifying target stimuli that appears where non-target stimuli appeared previously. TS subjects exhibit diminished NP

span.label: PRIMING AS A PROGNOSTIC INDEX - `their NP levels PREDICT THEIR RESPONSE TO BEHAVIORAL THERAPY`. Not a phenomenon under study, not an instrument for probing representations, but a clinical measurement used to forecast treatment outcome. A fourth job for the word in this corpus, alongside phenomenon, instrument and paradigm
span.quote: Individuals with Tourette syndrome (TS) exhibit deficits in inhibitory information processing which may reflect impaired neural mechanisms underlying symptoms and can be detected using a negative priming (NP) task. NP is the normal reduction of performance when identifying target stimuli that appears where non-target stimuli appeared previously. TS subjects exhibit diminished NP and their NP levels predict their response to behavioral therapy

span.label: THE EFFECT ONLY APPEARS UNDER CHALLENGE, which is a fact about the animal model rather than about the animals: `during the SHORT PRIME CHALLENGE, rats exhibited lower accuracy in NP vs. baseline trials`. A 0.25 s prime was needed to make the phenomenon measurable at all, and the same duration was then carried into the drug study. A translational model whose sensitivity had to be engineered into the timing
span.quote: During the short prime challenge, rats exhibited lower accuracy in NP vs. baseline trials, indicative of inhibitory information processing. Modulation by amphetamine administration indicates that this drug had rate-dependent effects

span.label: builds-on → the human visuospatial priming task of Tipper (1985) and Swerdlow et al. (1996)
span.quote: In this study, we aimed to describe the characteristics and heuristic values of a novel rat negative visuospatial priming paradigm ( Figure 1 ), based on a well-established human visuospatial priming task ( Swerdlow et al., 1996 ; Tipper, 1985 ).

span.label: negative priming —operationalised-as→ inhibitory information processing
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — The measurement claim the whole paper rests on: a deficit in inhibitory processing `can be detected using a negative priming task`, so the loss of performance is read as the mechanism working. Direction matters - the effect is the INDEX and the inhibitory process is what it indexes, not the other way round.
span.quote: Individuals with Tourette syndrome (TS) exhibit deficits in inhibitory information processing which may reflect impaired neural mechanisms underlying symptoms and can be detected using a negative priming (NP) task. NP is the normal reduction of performance when identifying target stimuli that appears where non-target stimuli appeared previously. TS subjects exhibit diminished NP and their NP levels predict their response to behavioral therapy

span.label: Tourette syndrome —causes→ negative priming
span.note: direction on the measure: reduces · strength of the relation: 0.9 — `reduces` is correct and reads backwards without the sense rows: the reduction is a reduction OF A REDUCTION. Negative priming is itself a performance loss, and Tourette patients show LESS of it - so less priming is the pathological direction here.
span.quote: Individuals with Tourette syndrome (TS) exhibit deficits in inhibitory information processing which may reflect impaired neural mechanisms underlying symptoms and can be detected using a negative priming (NP) task. NP is the normal reduction of performance when identifying target stimuli that appears where non-target stimuli appeared previously. TS subjects exhibit diminished NP and their NP levels predict their response to behavioral therapy

span.label: prime duration —causes→ negative priming
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.85 — Shortening the prime makes the effect bigger, which is why 0.25 s was carried into the drug study. Weighted 0.85: the sentence reports the choice retrospectively as a reason for a design decision rather than presenting the duration comparison as a result.
span.quote: Because the shortened 0.25 s prime stimulus duration produced the most robust negative priming in the previous experiments, this prime duration was used during the amphetamine challenge days

span.label: interaction effect (factorial analysis)
span.quote: Accuracy in the task exhibited significant interactions between trial type, AMPH dose, and negative priming levels in the drug-free state.

span.label: correlation
span.quote: Individual accuracy priming values during the two decreased prime duration challenges were significantly positively correlated

span.label: Latin square counterbalanced design
span.quote: Each rat received each dose of amphetamine following a Latin square design ( Dénes and Keedwell, 1974 ), which counterbalanced the order of all doses to minimize the risk of confounding order effects.

span.label: Rats trained on the new task showed a robust negative priming effect, performing worse when the target appeared where the distractor had just been.
span.quote: In the studies reported here, rats exhibited robust negative visuospatial priming, reflected by degraded performance when the targets were presented in the location previously occupied by the non-target distractor during the preceding prime (NP trials), compared to unrelated target locations in prime and probe trial (baseline trials).

span.label: The authors report this as the first rodent paradigm measuring visuospatial priming.
span.quote: To our knowledge, this is the first documented rat task assessing visuospatial priming.

span.label: Shortening the prime from 0.5 s to 0.25 s strengthened the negative priming effect.
span.quote: Shorter prime duration resulted in accuracy priming values becoming more positive compared to the days before and after the challenge, indicating a stronger NP effect

span.label: Lengthening the prime from 0.5 s to 1 s weakened negative priming, the mirror image of the short-prime result.
span.quote: This pattern – that the priming effect became stronger when the prime duration was reduced – was consistent with the observation that lengthening the prime duration from 0.5 to 1 s weakened the priming effect

span.label: Each animal's degree of negative priming was consistent across two repetitions of the short-prime challenge, suggesting NP is a stable individual trait.
span.quote: indicating that the degree of NP in this task appears to be a stable trait inherent to the animal

span.label: Amphetamine abolished negative priming at every dose in rats that showed strong drug-free priming.
span.quote: Significant NP was observed in high NP rats after saline administration, but was abolished in these rats after AMPH administration at all doses.

span.label: In rats the negative priming effect appeared in accuracy rather than in response latency, unlike the human task where latency is the more robust index.
span.quote: The negative priming effect reported here was most robustly observed in response accuracy: significantly lower accuracy was detected in NP trials compared to baseline trials

span.label: Amphetamine reliably increased premature responding at all doses, while leaving trials completed unaffected.
span.quote: Premature responses were increased significantly by all doses of AMPH

span.label: negative priming (NP)
span.quote: NP is the normal reduction of performance when identifying target stimuli that appears where non-target stimuli appeared previously.

span.label: inhibitory information processing
span.quote: impairments in inhibitory information processing, defined as the ability to suppress reactions to irrelevant or inappropriate information, may contribute to symptoms of conditions characterized by repetitive or otherwise disordered stimulus-driven behaviors

span.label: negative priming trial versus baseline trial
span.term: negative priming trial versus baseline trial
span.quote: When the target stimulus in a probe is presented in the same location as the non-target stimulus in the preceding prime (“negative priming trial”), healthy subjects exhibit slower reaction times and lower accuracy compared to probes in which target location is unrelated to non-target location during the prime (“baseline trial”)

span.label: accuracy priming value
span.quote: Accuracy priming value : difference in accuracy between baseline and NP trials (average accuracy during baseline trials - average accuracy during NP trials).

span.label: correct response latency priming value
span.quote: Correct response latency priming value : difference in correct response latency between baseline and NP trials (average correct response latency during baseline trials - average correct response latency during NP trials).

span.label: high NP and low NP rats
span.term: high NP and low NP rats
span.quote: identifying “high NP” rats (accuracy priming values above 0 on the day of saline treatment) and “low NP” rats (accuracy priming values below 0 on the day of saline treatment)

span.label: convergent validity (of animal models)
span.quote: By modeling several symptoms of TS, however, any compounds developed that attenuate deficits in several of these models are more likely to be efficacious in patients, a concept referred to as convergent validity.

span.label: prime stimulus duration
span.quote: rats were challenged by decreasing the duration of the prime stimuli from 0.5 s to 0.25 s.

span.label: d-amphetamine dose
span.quote: Rats then received 0, 0.25, 0.5, or 1 mg/kg D-amphetamine 10 min before being tested in the negative visuospatial priming task.

span.label: trial type (baseline versus negative priming)
span.quote: In half of the trials, the target stimulus during the probe was located in the aperture that had contained no visual stimulus during the prime ( baseline trials ).

span.label: response accuracy
span.quote: Accuracy : number of correct responses divided by the sum of correct responses, incorrect responses, and false alarms

span.label: latency to correct response
span.quote: Latency to correct response : time from the onset of the light stimulus to the performance of a correct nosepoke response.

span.label: premature responses
span.quote: Premature responses were increased significantly by all doses of AMPH

span.label: drug-free negative priming level (high NP versus low NP)
span.term: drug-free negative priming level (high NP versus low NP)
span.quote: Accuracy priming values likewise exhibited significant interactions between AMPH dose and priming levels in the drug-free state, with high NP and low NP rats differing in their priming values only after saline administration.

span.label: body weight under food restriction
span.quote: Food restriction was calibrated to keep rats at 90% of their free-feeding weight and continued throughout behavioral testing.

span.label: 13 of 16 — final sample after three rats failed to reach stable task performance and were excluded
span.quote: Three of 16 rats failed to develop stable performance in the task and were excluded, leading to a final n of 13 rats.

span.label: 0, 0.25, 0.5, or 1 mg/kg — d-amphetamine doses given subcutaneously 10 min before testing, in a counterbalanced within-subject design
span.quote: Rats then received 0, 0.25, 0.5, or 1 mg/kg D-amphetamine 10 min before being tested in the negative visuospatial priming task.

span.label: 0.5 s to 0.25 s — the reduction in prime stimulus duration that produced the most robust negative priming
span.quote: rats were challenged by decreasing the duration of the prime stimuli from 0.5 s to 0.25 s.

span.label: 5 Hz — flicker rate of the non-target distractor light, distinguishing it from the continuous target light
span.quote: the target stimulus (a continuous light) and the non-target distractor stimulus (a 5 Hz flashing light) were presented in two of the response apertures

span.label: 0.5 s for seven rats, 0.75 s for three rats, 1 s for one rat, and 1.5 s for two rats — the shortest probe stimulus duration each rat could sustain at criterion performance
span.quote: The final probe stimulus duration achieved was 0.5 s for seven rats, 0.75 s for three rats, 1 s for one rat, and 1.5 s for two rats.

span.label: around 15 sessions — average training needed to reach criterion on the visual discrimination stage
span.quote: On average, rats required around 15 sessions to reach criterion performance.

span.label: 90% — proportion of free-feeding body weight at which rats were maintained by food restriction throughout testing
span.quote: Food restriction was calibrated to keep rats at 90% of their free-feeding weight and continued throughout behavioral testing.
